events.summary: Fix only what code can fix: bump the indirect x/mod dependency (pulled in by github.com/google/go-licenses/v2, not by agent code) and add a top-level read-only permissions block to the two workflows that lacked one. Every job that publishes already declares its own job-level permissions, so the top-level default does not remove any grant. Not touched: the job-level contents: write grants (release-binaries, helm-release, release-manifest, release-bundle, update-changelog, dependabot-licenses commit) are required to create releases and push commits; branch protection, code-review, and the CII badge are repository settings, not workflow content.

Reproduced both findings locally before changing anything: go.mod pinned golang.org/x/mod v0.37.0 (indirect; 'go mod why -m' traces it to github.com/google/go-licenses/v2), and 'go list -m -versions' confirmed v0.40.0 is the current release matching the advisories' fixed version. The failing Image Scan job log on Dependabot PR #163 (run 34071322793) exits 1 from the Trivy image step at severity HIGH,CRITICAL. For the workflow alerts, an awk pass over ci.yaml and release.yaml showed no top-level 'permissions:' key while dependabot-licenses.yaml, e2e-airgap.yaml, agent-behavior.yml and scorecard.yml all had one, matching Scorecard's per-file findings exactly.

go get golang.org/x/mod@v0.40.0 && go mod tidy (also moved x/net v0.58.0, x/text v0.41.0, x/tools v0.49.0 as transitive minimums). Added 'permissions: contents: read' at the top level of ci.yaml and release.yaml with a comment explaining that publishing jobs widen it per job.

go build ./... clean; gofmt -l . empty; go vet ./... clean; go test ./... all 15 packages pass; scripts/ci/check-mutable-inputs.py passes for the three workflows; PyYAML parses both edited workflows; actionlint reports only the two pre-existing shellcheck style notes (same count on main); local 'trivy fs --scanners vuln --severity HIGH,CRITICAL .' reports 0 findings for go.mod.
events.scope: Local static checks and unit tests plus a local Trivy filesystem scan. Does NOT prove the CI Image Scan job (which scans the built image) passes or that Scorecard re-scores the Token-Permissions check -- both require the next CI/Scorecard run on GitHub.

events.summary: In-repo fixes for the x/mod CVEs and the missing top-level workflow permissions are done and verified locally. Remaining alerts need either an explicit dismissal with justification (job-level contents: write on release/commit jobs) or repository-settings changes (branch protection on main, required reviews, CII badge enrolment), which are the maintainer's decision.
